doc: The edits of spec 085 (User Story 2, SC-002) on a stream of three documents with three comments: a target changed, a window changed, an objective added, an SLO added, and an SLI removed and the removal undone. Every byte no edit concerns stays as it was, every comment included.

steps.doc: Opening and saving without an edit writes the bytes that were read: three documents, their --- lines and the three comments.
steps.expect:
# Checkout's service level objectives, kept beside its code.
apiVersion: openslo/v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: checkout
  displayName: Checkout
---
# Errors seen at the load balancer.
apiVersion: openslo/v1
kind: SLI
metadata:
  name: checkout-errors
spec:
  ratioMetric:
    good:
      metricSource:
        type: Prometheus
        spec:
          query: sum(rate(lb_requests_total{code!~"5.."}[5m]))
    total:
      metricSource:
        type: Prometheus
        spec:
          query: sum(rate(lb_requests_total[5m]))
---
apiVersion: openslo/v1
kind: SLO
metadata:
  name: checkout-availability
  displayName: Checkout availability
spec:
  service: checkout
  indicatorRef: checkout-errors
  timeWindow:
    - duration: 28d # four weeks, rolling
      isRolling: true
  budgetingMethod: Occurrences
  objectives:
    - displayName: Available
      target: 0.99 # agreed with the product owner

steps.doc: A set of the objective's target (the model's targetRatio, persistence.typeMap) replaces the number alone, written as the shortest form that reads back as it (number: shortest); the comment after it on the line stays.

steps.doc: A set of the SLO's window, its first timeWindow item's duration, replaces 28d with 7d; isRolling and the comment stay, so the window reads 7d rolling and the budget the diagram shows follows (openslo-slo.md, Budget). The comment still says four weeks: no edit rewrites a comment.

steps.doc: An add of an objective to the SLO is an insert after its last objective, the line span of that item, which ends the body: a new sequence item at that item's indentation, its keys in the binding's order (displayName, then target).

steps.doc: An add of an SLO is an insert at the root (FBL 0.22, section 6.2): one insert-entry at the end of the body, a --- line and the document at indentation 0, apiVersion and kind its constants in the places keys gives them, metadata holding the name and spec the attributes the add gives in the order of their bindings (service, indicatorRef, budgetingMethod), then the rule's skeleton, a 28-day rolling window. The diagram's tool adds its first objective as a second step (behavior, addSlo).
